mechanical.notes: Attempt-1 FAIL (hero-rack camera aimed at a wall; office context framed behind the lens) fixed and superseded. Both were the SAME root: a view was framed by the SCENE it lives in, not by what it must SHOW. (1) The hero-rack solver used all six cabinets as the framing subject, so the detail view backed up to contain the whole row (eye x=5.30 past the x=2.44 corridor end) and its centre ray hit wall_right; now each view frames its OWN subject (detail -> rack_equipment). (2) The aisle camera at azimuth 12 stood at the lounge end looking away (dot -0.89), ending on a wall; fixed to azimuth 192 (the site-01/05 viewpoint). THREE more defects surfaced: FOV belongs to the view (a 2 m stack in a 2 m aisle needs a wide lens; fov 50 aisle / 75 detail, since the geometry left no other play), the solver could pass through walls (radius now capped at 2.4 m for detail), and — the sharpest — verifyCriticalsAreVisible HAD THE SAME BUG IT WAS WRITTEN TO CATCH: it tested only whether a RAY REACHED each critical, and a ray to an object BEHIND the camera arrives fine, so it fired on hero-through-wall but stayed MUTE on aisle-aimed-away. REACHABILITY IS NOT FRAMING; it now requires BOTH (inside the frustum AND unobstructed through transparent surfaces). The must-show list is derived from the DECLARED criticals, which correctly removed two entries added by taste (the glass partition — transparent by design, satisfied by seeing the lounge THROUGH it; the ceiling light panels — real but not a declared critical, so not asserted). Negative control: azimuth 12 -> lounge out of frame; azimuth 68 -> four devices blocked by wall_right; as-is zero. Assembly unchanged and headless-verified: 6 cabinets, 569/1200 draws, integer-U seating, 0 assembly-guard failures; console/boot/offline clean.

notes: Inline orchestrator judgment; supersedes attempt-1. Strong recovery: both blockers were bounded camera fixes rooted in one idea — a view is defined by what it must SHOW, not by the scene it sits in — and fixing them surfaced a fov-per-view rule, a wall-clipping radius cap, and the sharpest finding of the pass: a visibility guard that measured reachability (a ray can reach an object behind the camera) instead of FRAMING, so it could not see the very framing defect it existed for. The hero-rack now reads the populated rack with the red/blue dual-feed PDU pair, the aisle now reads the lounge/pendant/glass-wall office context, and all five criticals are judgeable and pass. The assembly itself (six assets, one three.js instance, integer-U seating, the cross-asset-divergence guards) was already sound. Cleared to the structural pass.
